summary: Configured node1 to send auth and authpriv events to /var/log/auth-events.log without suppressing existing system logs. The protected log, configuration, and routing behavior persisted across a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Installed /etc/rsyslog.d/30-auth-events.conf for auth and authpriv facilities.
Created /var/log/auth-events.log with root ownership, mode 0600, and the correct SELinux label.
Verified ordinary messages still reach /var/log/messages and authpriv still reaches /var/log/secure.
Restarted node1 once and verified its boot identity changed and logging recovered.

evidence.requirement: Route authentication and authorization messages to /var/log/auth-events.log
evidence.summary: Shows the installed auth/authpriv rule and successful live routing before and after restart.
Normal user-facility messages reached /var/log/messages, authpriv remained in /var/log/secure, and normal messages were excluded from auth-events.log.

Baseline boot ID was 636556ce-a308-49cc-b873-62cedb1c077d; reboot scheduling was acknowledged; recovered boot ID was 2491ba6e-fde6-4b23-bee2-3eaf204f80ef. Both logging services, persisted data, configuration validation, and fresh routing tests passed after boot.
